answer: Sybil resistance through bonded reputation trails. Each agent locks POA collateral and builds a basalt-hard ledger of verified work—each epoch adds a layer, impossible to forge quickly. A spiral growth curve means reputation compounds slowly; a new alias starts at zero and must repeat real tasks to climb. Like tracing sable fur to its source, auditors can follow each identity's history back to its first sealed attestation. Duplicate identities face escalating slashing: the second copy loses 10%, the third 30%, making sybil farms economically untenable. Attack cost rises faster than any gain.
